subject: Clarifying SIG item about multitenant audit scope (Q12)
messages:
From: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finserv.io
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for returning our SIG in advance of our audit. One of our reviewers flagged item Q12 ("Describe how you support customer audit requests related to multi-tenant environments and evidence of logical separation"). The reviewer is unsure whether you consider tenant separation controls that are "logical" (namespace/KV isolation and per-customer encryption keys) sufficient, or if they require a dedicated physical environment for FinServ's data.

Could you provide a written interpretation that we can include in our audit notes, plus any evidence you can attach (network diagrams, SOC 2 excerpts, etc.)? We're aiming to close the loop by next Friday.

Attached: FinServ_SIG_Q&A_v1.pdf (our copy of the questionnaire with redlines).

Thanks,
Alex
Security Engineering — FinServ Corp
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Alex — thanks for the note and the patience. Quick answer: logical separation with cryptographic tenant keys and RBAC-backed control plane is our standard for hosted deployments; we also offer Dedicated/Private options when customers require physical isolation.

That said, for auditability we should provide: (1) a concise written interpretation you can include in your audit package, (2) a network/architecture diagram showing tenant isolation boundaries, and (3) SOC 2 control excerpts that map to the SIG question.

Marissa — looping you in to confirm the evidence bundle and whether legal needs to sign the statement. Karthik — can you pull the network diagram and SOC2 excerpt?

I'll follow up with a call invite in case Alex prefers a short sync.

— Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Alex — thanks for flagging. Short timeline: we can produce the written interpretation and evidence by Thursday. A couple of points to make sure our wording fits your audit:

- "Logical separation" in our context means per-tenant encryption keys at rest, namespace-based runtime isolation, and enforcement of tenant-level ACLs in our control plane.
- We map those controls to SOC 2 CC6 (logical and physical access controls) and to relevant SIG fields. See the attached network-segmentation-diagram.pdf and SOC2-CC6-excerpt.pdf.

If the auditor requires dedicated physical hosts, we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or a Dedicated pool with contractual isolation; we can note that as an option rather than our default.

I'm attaching the draft written statement below as a text file; please tell us if you need legal sign-off. If it's acceptable, we can provide a signed letterhead statement as well.

Attachments (stubs): network-segmentation-diagram.pdf, SOC2-CC6-excerpt.pdf

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
From: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finserv.io
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups:

1) For the audit notes we need a single paragraph statement answering Q12 directly (yes/no + short rationale) that the auditor can reference.
2) Please confirm whether encryption keys are customer-specific and the KMS tenancy model (do we control the CMK or can FinServ supply a customer-managed CMK?).
3) If you can provide a signed PDF on Redwood letterhead that would be ideal.

Can you confirm by EOD Thursday?

-Alex
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Alex — quick technical confirmation: encryption at rest uses per-tenant DEKs (data encryption keys) wrapped by a tenant-specific KMS key. For hosted customers we can support either Redwood-managed CMKs or customer-supplied CMKs in supported clouds (customer-supplied requires configured KMS access and may have onboarding lead time).

Network and runtime isolation: tenant workloads run in logically separated namespaces with network policies that enforce egress/ingress controls; we publish the segmentation diagram (attached).

Let us know if you need the KMS config examples; happy to redact specific ARNs for the audit copy.

— Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform Security
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex M. (FinServ Security) <alex.m@finserv.io>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q12 — multitenant audit scope (need clarification)

Alex — per your request, here is the single-paragraph statement you can include in audit notes. We can provide this on letterhead if needed: 

"Redwood Inference considers logical tenant separation with customer-scoped encryption and enforced control-plane ACLs to satisfy the requirements referenced in SIG item Q12 for hosted deployments. For customers requiring physical isolation, Redwood offers Dedicated and Private deployment options which provide hardware-level tenancy segregation by contract. For hosted deployments, tenant data is encrypted with per-tenant data encryption keys wrapped by tenant-specific CMKs; customers may supply their own CMKs where required."
Attached: redwood-signed-statement-q12.txt (we will convert to signed PDF on request).

Please confirm acceptance or ask for edits and note whether you want Redwood legal to sign.

Thanks,
Marissa
